question: With a fresh synthetic fixture and correctly globalized step-loss metric, do pinned base and PR #7249 candidate produce the same pooled-token SGD update when run through the real Transformers Trainer.train loop, Accelerate.backward, and two-process CPU Gloo DDP?
v4_reason: V1 and v2 were harness setup failures. V3 completed base Trainer updates but its local DataLoaders bypassed Accelerator data dispatch, so TrainerOutput.training_loss was rank-local. V4 uses fresh token counts/advantages and freezes the primary scalar as the all-reduced mean of the rank-local losses returned by the actual Trainer.training_step calls. TrainerOutput loss is retained as a local diagnostic only.

estimand.loss: L is the sum of clipped GRPO token losses over all active completion tokens across ranks and microbatches divided by the total active completion-token count.
estimand.primary_loss_measure: Sum actual Trainer.training_step return values within each rank for the update; all_reduce SUM across ranks then divide by world size; compare to the direct pooled-token oracle.
estimand.parameter_update: One SGD step, lr=0.1, no weight decay/clipping, against the same-initialized model updated from direct pooled-token oracle gradient.
estimand.controls: Same local deterministic model; prompt/context positions masked; beta=0; no auxiliary loss.

scope.tested_path: Pinned AsyncGRPOTrainer.compute_loss/get_batch_samples + Transformers Trainer.train/_inner_training_loop/training_step + Accelerate.backward + real Gloo DDP reducer/no_sync + SGD optimizer and scheduler step.
scope.input_path: Rank-local deterministic DataLoaders constructed from production DataCollatorForRollout outputs. Production asynchronous worker, planner, and DataLoaderDispatcher are replaced/bypassed.
scope.prior_evidence: VARE DDP v2 used actual reducer but direct backward/manual SGD; PR-authored tests use Trainer.train single-process and simulated rank aggregation.

claim_limits: This remains a synthetic trainer-correctness result, not a model capability or task-success result.
Inputs bypass the production async worker and Accelerator DataLoaderDispatcher.
The upstream PR already contains the normalization fix; this is additional test evidence, not an original fix or novelty claim.
